headline: High-risk pair: LightAgent’s broad network/MCP surface can leak or misroute data, while LlamaFactory’s local-only profile limits direct interaction but not downstream misuse.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LightAgent can use MCP and browsers, so it may ingest external content and tool outputs; LlamaFactory has no MCP, filesystem, or browser surface, so it is not a direct injection bridge. The pair still has a plausible path if LightAgent’s outputs are copied into LlamaFactory workflows, but that is not default. Uncertainty favors medium over low because LightAgent’s shared tool surfaces are broad.
conditions: IF LightAgent forwards browser or MCP content into LlamaFactory prompts without sanitization, injection becomes actionable.
IF an operator manually copies LightAgent output into LlamaFactory input, prompt injection can traverse the pair.
mitigations: Disable MCP sources that are not trusted.
Strip instructions from LightAgent outputs before reuse.
Use a fixed prompt template for LlamaFactory inputs.
Add a human review step for any copied content.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: LightAgent touches conversations, memory, tool results, and secrets, and has broad network egress; LlamaFactory is local-only with no filesystem read/write or egress. The pair can still leak if LightAgent sends sensitive context to external APIs, but LlamaFactory itself does not add a second exfiltration path. This is medium because sensitive data is clearly present on one side and default networked inference is enabled there.
conditions: IF LightAgent processes user conversations or secrets through external APIs, those data may leave the local boundary.
IF LlamaFactory is fed copied sensitive outputs from LightAgent, the pair can expose them in downstream logs or prompts.
mitigations: Route LightAgent through a local-only model for sensitive tasks.
Redact secrets before any external API call.
Turn off unnecessary logging in both agents.
Keep LlamaFactory isolated from copied sensitive transcripts.
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention filters on LightAgent egress.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LightAgent supports multiple instances and broad network/tool use, while LlamaFactory cannot write files, modify git, or use MCP. There is little direct write-write overlap, so conflict risk is limited unless an external orchestrator gives both access to the same mutable resource. Because that shared resource is not documented, the safer choice is low rather than none.
conditions: IF both agents are granted the same writable workspace by an external orchestrator, concurrent edits can conflict.
IF LightAgent is configured to write artifacts that LlamaFactory also consumes, race conditions may appear.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Avoid concurrent runs on shared artifacts.
Serialize any handoff between agents.
Use read-only mounts for LlamaFactory.
requires-engineering: add lock files or transactional writes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: LightAgent can produce tool results and workflow state that may be treated as authoritative, while LlamaFactory is a downstream model framework that could render or act on copied outputs. The pair lacks documented verification or provenance controls, so errors can cascade if LightAgent’s outputs are reused uncritically. This is medium because the pathway exists in common workflows even though direct action authority is not shown.
conditions: IF LlamaFactory consumes LightAgent outputs without verification, hallucinations or bad tool results can propagate.
IF LightAgent emits malformed provenance metadata, downstream decisions may be based on false confidence.
mitigations: Require source verification before reuse.
Compare LightAgent outputs against original inputs.
Add a rejection rule for missing provenance.
Keep a manual approval step for consequential actions.
requires-engineering: implement structured validation between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: LightAgent handles user conversations, long-term memory, trace data, and secrets, while LlamaFactory’s profile shows no data classes or compliance controls. That mismatch creates a plausible retention/residency/compliance gap if the same regulated data flows through both. Because only LightAgent’s handling is documented, uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF regulated data such as secrets or personal data is routed from LightAgent into LlamaFactory logs or prompts, compliance obligations may be violated.
IF retention or deletion requirements apply to LightAgent memory but not to LlamaFactory artifacts, subject-rights handling can diverge.
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data into LlamaFactory.
Minimize LightAgent memory retention.
Document retention rules for both agents.
Purge transcripts after use.
requires-engineering: align compliance controls and retention policies.
